discovery: Prediction and observational discovery of magnetars, neutron stars powered by ultra-strong magnetic fields

nominees.name: Robert C. Duncan
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Christopher Thompson
nominees.affiliation: Canadian Institute for Theoretical Astrophysics, University of Toronto, Canada

motivation: Duncan and Thompson predicted in 1992 that dynamo action in newborn neutron stars can produce magnetic fields of 10^14-10^15 gauss, far above the quantum critical field, and that the decay of these fields could power soft gamma repeaters and anomalous X-ray pulsars. In 1998 Kouveliotou and collaborators measured the spin period and spin-down of SGR 1806-20 with RXTE. The result implied a dipole field of about 10^15 G and confirmed the magnetar model. Magnetars are now an established class of neutron stars. They are laboratories for physics in extreme fields, including vacuum birefringence and photon splitting. They explain giant flares, and the 2020 detection of a fast radio burst from SGR 1935+2154 linked them to fast radio bursts. The work shows how bold theory and precise high-energy measurement together open a new window on matter under extreme conditions.
